devdoc.details: Library for computing storage (and transient storage) locations from namespaces and deriving slots corresponding to standard patterns. The derivation method for array and mapping matches the storage layout used by the solidity language / compiler. See https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/v0.8.20/internals/layout_in_storage.html#mappings-and-dynamic-arrays[Solidity docs for mappings and dynamic arrays.]. Example usage: ```solidity contract Example {     // Add the library methods     using StorageSlot for bytes32;     using SlotDerivation for bytes32;     // Declare a namespace     string private constant _NAMESPACE = "<namespace>"; // eg. OpenZeppelin.Slot     function setValueInNamespace(uint256 key, address newValue) internal {         _NAMESPACE.erc7201Slot().deriveMapping(key).getAddressSlot().value = newValue;     }     function getValueInNamespace(uint256 key) internal view returns (address) {         return _NAMESPACE.erc7201Slot().deriveMapping(key).getAddressSlot().value;     } } ``` TIP: Consider using this library along with {StorageSlot}. NOTE: This library provides a way to manipulate storage locations in a non-standard way. Tooling for checking upgrade safety will ignore the slots accessed through this library. _Available since v5.1._

devdoc.details: Library for reading and writing primitive types to specific storage slots. Storage slots are often used to avoid storage conflict when dealing with upgradeable contracts. This library helps with reading and writing to such slots without the need for inline assembly. The functions in this library return Slot structs that contain a `value` member that can be used to read or write. Example usage to set ERC-1967 implementation slot: ```solidity contract ERC1967 {     // Define the slot. Alternatively, use the SlotDerivation library to derive the slot.     bytes32 internal constant _IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT = 0x360894a13ba1a3210667c828492db98dca3e2076cc3735a920a3ca505d382bbc;     function _getImplementation() internal view returns (address) {         return StorageSlot.getAddressSlot(_IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT).value;     }     function _setImplementation(address newImplementation) internal {         require(newImplementation.code.length > 0);         StorageSlot.getAddressSlot(_IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT).value = newImplementation;     } } ``` TIP: Consider using this library along with {SlotDerivation}.

devdoc.details: Wrappers over Solidity's uintXX/intXX/bool casting operators with added overflow checks. Downcasting from uint256/int256 in Solidity does not revert on overflow. This can easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows. Using this library instead of the unchecked operations eliminates an entire class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.

SafeCastOverflowedIntDowncast(uint8,int2.details: Value doesn't fit in an int of `bits` size.

SafeCastOverflowedIntToUint(int256).details: An int value doesn't fit in an uint of `bits` size.

SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast(uint8,uin.details: Value doesn't fit in an uint of `bits` size.

SafeCastOverflowedUintToInt(uint256).details: An uint value doesn't fit in an int of `bits` size.

devdoc.details: Library for managing https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(abstract_data_type)[sets] of primitive types. Sets have the following properties: - Elements are added, removed, and checked for existence in constant time (O(1)). - Elements are enumerated in O(n). No guarantees are made on the ordering. - Set can be cleared (all elements removed) in O(n). ```solidity contract Example {     // Add the library methods     using EnumerableSet for EnumerableSet.AddressSet;     // Declare a set state variable     EnumerableSet.AddressSet private mySet; } ``` The following types are supported: - `bytes32` (`Bytes32Set`) since v3.3.0 - `address` (`AddressSet`) since v3.3.0 - `uint256` (`UintSet`) since v3.3.0 - `string` (`StringSet`) since v5.4.0 - `bytes` (`BytesSet`) since v5.4.0 [WARNING] ==== Trying to delete such a structure from storage will likely result in data corruption, rendering the structure unusable. See https://github.com/ethereum/solidity/pull/11843[ethereum/solidity#11843] for more info. In order to clean an EnumerableSet, you can either remove all elements one by one or create a fresh instance using an array of EnumerableSet. ====

getRoleCount().details: Returns the number of roles stored in the contract.

getRoleMemberCount(bytes32).details: Returns the number of members of the specified role.

returns._0: The number of members of the role.

getRoleMembers(bytes32,uint256,uint256).details: Returns the members of the specified role.

params.end: the end index, the value for this index will not be included.
params.start: the start index, the value for this index will be included.

getRoles(uint256,uint256).details: Returns the keys of the roles stored in the contract.

params.end: The ending index of the range of roles to return.
params.start: The starting index of the range of roles to return.

grantRole(address,bytes32).details: Grants the specified role to the given account.

params.roleKey: The key of the role to grant.

hasRole(address,bytes32).details: Returns true if the given account has the specified role.

returns._0: True if the account has the role, false otherwise.

revokeRole(address,bytes32).details: Revokes the specified role from the given account.

params.roleKey: The key of the role to revoke.

devdoc.details: Uses GMX Oracle contract instead of Chainlink, works for all tokens supported by GMXGMX Oracle already provides prices in 30 decimal format

params.isIncrease: True for opening/increasing, false for closing/decreasing
params.isLong: True for long position, false for short

returns.currentPrice: Current market price in GMX format (30 decimals)

getAcceptablePrice(address,bool,bool,uin.details: Logic based on GMX's BaseOrderUtils.sol:      - INCREASE LONG: acceptablePrice is MAX price you'll pay (current + slippage)      - INCREASE SHORT: acceptablePrice is MIN price you'll accept (current - slippage)      - DECREASE LONG: acceptablePrice is MIN price you'll accept (executionPrice >= acceptablePrice)                       Due to price impact, it's safer to use 0 or a very low value      - DECREASE SHORT: acceptablePrice is MAX price you'll pay (executionPrice <= acceptablePrice)                       Due to price impact, it's safer to use max or a very high value IMPORTANT: For decrease orders, GMX validates that:      - LONG decrease: executionPrice >= acceptablePrice (acceptablePrice is MINIMUM)      - SHORT decrease: executionPrice <= acceptablePrice (acceptablePrice is MAXIMUM)            Price impact can make executionPrice worse than expected, so use conservative values      or use minOutputAmount for better slippage control on decrease orders.

params.isIncrease: True for opening/increasing, false for closing/decreasing
params.isLong: True for long position, false for short
params.useConservativeDecrease: If true, uses 0 (LONG) or max (SHORT) for decrease orders

returns.currentPrice: Current market price in GMX format (30 decimals)

params.isIncrease: True for opening/increasing, false for closing/decreasing
params.isLong: True for long position, false for short

returns.currentPrice: Current market price in GMX format (30 decimals)

getExpectedOutputUsd(bytes32,address,uin.details: Uses GMX Reader to get real-time position info and calculate expected outputThis is an approximation. Actual output may vary due to price impact and fees

params.sizeDeltaUsd: Size to decrease in USD (30 decimals), use 0 for full position

returns.expectedOutputUsd: Expected output value in USD (30 decimals)

returns.maxPrice: Maximum price from GMX Oracle (30 decimals)
returns.midPrice: Mid price (average) from GMX Oracle (30 decimals)
returns.minPrice: Minimum price from GMX Oracle (30 decimals)

returns.longTokenPrice: Price of long collateral token (30 decimals)
returns.shortTokenPrice: Price of short collateral token (30 decimals)

returns.indexToken: Address of the index token (e.g., WETH for ETH/USD market)
returns.longToken: Address of the long collateral token
returns.shortToken: Address of the short collateral token

getMinOutputAmount(uint256,uint256).details: For decrease orders, minOutputAmount is more reliable than acceptablePrice      because it validates the USD value received, not the execution price

params.expectedOutputUsd: Expected output value in USD (30 decimals)

returns.minOutputAmount: Minimum output amount in USD (30 decimals)

params.sizeDeltaUsd: Size to decrease in USD (30 decimals), use 0 for full position

returns.minOutputAmount: Minimum output amount in USD (30 decimals)

getPrice(address).details: Returns the mid price converted to 18 decimals for easier storage and readabilityUse getPriceIn30Decimals() if you need the full 30 decimal precision

returns.price: Current price from GMX Oracle (mid price, 18 decimals for storage)

getPriceForStorage(address).details: This function is useful for storing prices in position dataConverts from 30 decimals (GMX format) to 18 decimals for storage

getPriceIn30Decimals(address).details: Use this for calculations that require full precision

returns.price: Current price from GMX Oracle (mid price, 30 decimals)

devdoc.author: @Diego-AVZ
devdoc.custom:security: Designed to prevent single points of failure and admin compromise
devdoc.details: Implements multi-admin governance with contract whitelisting and admin managementFeatures: 3-initial admin setup, democratic contract approval, admin penalization system

allowContract(address,string).custom:security: Only admin addresses can whitelist contractsRequires 2 admin approvals for activation (prevents single admin compromise)
allowContract(address,string).details: Implements democratic consensus - requires 2 admin approvals to activate contractPrevents duplicate approvals from same admin. Contract activates when approvals >= 2

params._contract: The address of the contract to whitelist

params._admin2: The address of the second administrator
params._admin3: The address of the third administrator
params._mainAdmin: The address of the main administrator

deleteContract(address).custom:security: Only admin addresses can remove contracts from the protocol
deleteContract(address).details: Only callable by admin addresses. Sets the contract's protocol status to false

params._contract: The address of the contract to remove from the protocol

params._admin: The address of the admin to query

returns._0: Admin struct containing status, penalties, and who penalized them
Array of all admin addresses in the system
True if the address is a protocol contract, false otherwise

penalizeAdmin(address).custom:security: Prevents self-penalization and duplicate penalties from same adminAdmin is removed when penalties >= 2 (majority consensus)
penalizeAdmin(address).details: Implements democratic consensus - admin is removed when majority agrees

params._admin: The address of the admin to penalize

proposeAdmin(address).custom:security: Prevents single compromised admin from adding unlimited adminsRequires democratic consensus (2 approvals) to add new admin
proposeAdmin(address).details: Uses same approval system as contracts - requires 2 admin approvals

params._admin: The address of the new admin to propose

documentation.text: @dev Collection of functions related to array types.

@dev Sort an array of uint256 (in memory) following the provided comparator function.
 This function does the sorting "in place", meaning that it overrides the input. The object is returned for
 convenience, but that returned value can be discarded safely if the caller has a memory pointer to the array.
 NOTE: this function's cost is `O(n · log(n))` in average and `O(n²)` in the worst case, with n the length of the
 array. Using it in view functions that are executed through `eth_call` is safe, but one should be very careful
 when executing this as part of a transaction. If the array being sorted is too large, the sort operation may
 consume more gas than is available in a block, leading to potential DoS.
 IMPORTANT: Consider memory side-effects when using custom comparator functions that access memory in an unsafe way.

@dev Performs a quick sort of a segment of memory. The segment sorted starts at `begin` (inclusive), and stops
 at end (exclusive). Sorting follows the `comp` comparator.
 Invariant: `begin <= end`. This is the case when initially called by {sort} and is preserved in subcalls.
 IMPORTANT: Memory locations between `begin` and `end` are not validated/zeroed. This function should
 be used only if the limits are within a memory array.

@dev Searches a sorted `array` and returns the first index that contains
 a value greater or equal to `element`. If no such index exists (i.e. all
 values in the array are strictly less than `element`), the array length is
 returned. Time complexity O(log n).
 NOTE: The `array` is expected to be sorted in ascending order, and to
 contain no repeated elements.
 IMPORTANT: Deprecated. This implementation behaves as {lowerBound} but lacks
 support for repeated elements in the array. The {lowerBound} function should
 be used instead.

@dev Calculate the modular multiplicative inverse of a number in Z/nZ.
 If n is a prime, then Z/nZ is a field. In that case all elements are inversible, except 0.
 If n is not a prime, then Z/nZ is not a field, and some elements might not be inversible.
 If the input value is not inversible, 0 is returned.

 inverse using `Math.modExp(a, n - 2, n)`. See {invModPrime}.

@dev Variant of {invMod}. More efficient, but only works if `p` is known to be a prime greater than `2`.
 From https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_little_theorem[Fermat's little theorem], we know that if p is
 prime, then `a**(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p`. As a consequence, we have `a * a**(p-2) ≡ 1 mod p`, which means that
 `a**(p-2)` is the modular multiplicative inverse of a in Fp.
 NOTE: this function does NOT check that `p` is a prime greater than `2`.

 easily result in undesired exploitation or bugs, since developers usually
 assume that overflows raise errors. `SafeCast` restores this intuition by
 reverting the transaction when such an operation overflows.

 class of bugs, so it's recommended to use it always.

@dev Library for managing
 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(abstract_data_type)[sets] of primitive
 types.
 Sets have the following properties:
 - Elements are added, removed, and checked for existence in constant time
 (O(1)).
 - Elements are enumerated in O(n). No guarantees are made on the ordering.
 - Set can be cleared (all elements removed) in O(n).
 ```solidity
 contract Example {
     // Add the library methods
     using EnumerableSet for EnumerableSet.AddressSet;
     // Declare a set state variable
     EnumerableSet.AddressSet private mySet;
 }
 ```
 The following types are supported:
 - `bytes32` (`Bytes32Set`) since v3.3.0
 - `address` (`AddressSet`) since v3.3.0
 - `uint256` (`UintSet`) since v3.3.0
 - `string` (`StringSet`) since v5.4.0
 - `bytes` (`BytesSet`) since v5.4.0
 [WARNING]
 ====
 Trying to delete such a structure from storage will likely result in data corruption, rendering the structure
 unusable.
 See https://github.com/ethereum/solidity/pull/11843[ethereum/solidity#11843] for more info.
 In order to clean an EnumerableSet, you can either remove all elements one by one or create a fresh instance using an
 array of EnumerableSet.
 ====
